scenarios.answer:
Yes, specific community college courses transfer into the Sac State Computer Science major. Here are the approved mappings:

| Community College Course | Transfers To (Sac State) | Units |
|---|---|---|
| MATH 11 — Calculus I | MATH 30 — Calculus I | 4 |
| MATH 12 — Calculus II | MATH 31 — Calculus II | 4 |
| MATH 13 — Linear Algebra | MATH 35 — Linear Algebra | 3 |
| CIS 10 — Programming Concepts I | CSC 20 — Programming Concepts I | 3 |
| CIS 11 — Programming Concepts II | CSC 28 — Programming Concepts II | 3 |
| CIS 21 — Computer Architecture | CSC 35 — Computer Architecture | 3 |

A few important notes:
- Introductory courses like "CIS 1 — Introduction to Computers" do **not** transfer into the major.
- A maximum of 70 lower-division transfer units can apply to the degree.
- Upper-division CS core courses (CSC 130 and above) must be completed at Sac State.

Bring your transcript to the Academic Advising Center for an official evaluation.

**Sources:**
- [assist-articulation-cc-to-sacstate-cs.md, §Lower-Division Course Mapping]
- [sacstate-catalog-cs-2025.md, §Lower-Division Requirements]

Here's what the official policy document says about renewing your Cal Grant B award. To renew, you must meet **all** of the following requirements each year:

1. **Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP)**, which includes a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. [financial-aid-cal-grant-b-policy.md, §Renewal Requirements]
2. **Stay enrolled at least half-time** in an eligible program. [financial-aid-cal-grant-b-policy.md, §Renewal Requirements]
3. **Continue to meet the Cal Grant income and asset ceilings** for the award year. [financial-aid-cal-grant-b-policy.md, §Income and Asset Ceilings]
4. **File a renewal FAFSA** (or California Dream Act Application) by the March 2 priority deadline. [financial-aid-cal-grant-b-policy.md, §Renewal Requirements]
5. **Not exceed the maximum award eligibility period** (up to four years of full-time equivalent benefits). [financial-aid-cal-grant-b-policy.md, §Renewal Requirements]

Because BullBot doesn't have access to your personal student record, your individual renewal status and specific income ceilings must be confirmed with the Financial Aid & Scholarships Office. [advising-contacts.md, §Financial Aid]

**Sources:**

You can add the Data Science minor without delaying graduation by overlapping minor courses with your CS technical electives.

The minor requires 18 units, including:
- STAT 50 — Introduction to Probability and Statistics (3 units)
- CSC 177 — Data Mining and Analytics (3 units)
- STAT 115A — Statistical Computing (3 units)

Because **CSC 177 and STAT 115A also count as approved CS technical electives** [sacstate-catalog-cs-2025.md, §Technical Electives], taking them as your electives applies those units to both the major and the minor.

Suggested sequencing:
- **Term 1:** STAT 50 (take early — it is a prerequisite for several electives)
- **Term 2:** CSC 177 (counts as a CS technical elective)
- **Term 3:** STAT 115A (counts as a CS technical elective) + one approved minor elective

This keeps the extra units to a minimum. An advisor must confirm the final plan.

**Sources:**
- [data-science-minor-requirements.md, §Required Courses]
- [data-science-minor-requirements.md, §Overlap With Computer Science]
- [sacstate-catalog-cs-2025.md, §Technical Electives]
